sources.text: Important Contact Information Community-Related Emergencies Emergencies: For any life-threatening emergencies, please call 9-1-1. If you have a community-related emergency, such as an irrigation leak or community space safety hazards, please call the Resident Resource Center at 720-661-9694 and press 2 for after-hours emergency services. Service requests or issues: Please use the Sterling Ranch 311 app to report a service request or issue. sources.text: Trash & Recycling Our trash provider is Waste Connections. Waste Connections uses automated trucks to service Sterling Ranch and provide a more efficient trash and recycling experience. The new equipment features a side arm system that makes it easier to maneuver, ensures driver safety, and allows for faster service. Trash and recycling service fees are included in your monthly CAB bill. Pick Up Schedule Make sure to place bins outside by 7 am for trash collection. Containers for pickup may be placed on the street or alleyway on the morning of pickup and must be returned to an appropriately screened location by the end of the pickup day. Please be aware Sterling Ranch is home to various types of wildlife. Pro per trash cart storage is essential to the community and its inhabitants' safety. Extra or bulky items can be picked up by contacting Waste Connections at 303-288-2100. For Providence Village , trash is picked up weekly on Monday, and recycling is picked up every other Monday. For Ascent Village, trash is picked up weekly on Tuesday, and recycling is picked up every other Tuesday. For Prospect Village , trash is picked up weekly on Thursday, and recycling is picked up every other Thursday. Holiday Schedule Trash pickup will be delayed by one day for the following holidays: New Year's Day Memorial Day Independence Day Labor Day Thanksgiving Christmas Opt-In for Service Notifications Waste Connections also has an emergency phone call system that can notify residents in case of a delay or interruption in service. Service Notification Form New Homeowners Trash Cart Delivery Trash and recycling carts will be delivered to your home within ten days of closing.

sources.text: Recycling Right -- 1 of 13 -- Recycling Guidelines  Waste Connections uses a single stream recycling model.  All acceptable recycling materials can be placed in one container  No sorting required. -- 2 of 13 -- -- 3 of 13 -- Non-Recyclable Items  Chip Bags  Candy Wrappers  Napkins  Paper Plates  Tissues  Pizza Boxes  Plastic Grocery Bags -- 4 of 13 -- Where Your Recycling Goes?  From your home to the Recycling Center.  From the Recycling Center to the Manufacture.  From the Manufacture back to you. -- 5 of 13 -- Where Your Recycling Goes  Once your recycle has been cleaned and sorted inside your home and placed in your recycle container it is picked up by a Waste Connections recycle Truck and heads to EcoCycle. When the truck reaches EcoCycle it is put on a large conveyer belt and the sorting process starts. Plastic, paper products, metal and glass are sorted from each other. Once all the plastics have been sorted together, they are then sorted again by type. Plastic bottles used for water and soda go one way and milk containers go in another and so forth. This is done for paper, glass and metal as well. Once everything has been sorted, the different types of materials are bundled together in big cubs at a certain weight and are ready to be sold and shipped.  The cleaner the materials are the better. This allows for fewer issues with the sorting equipment and a better price. One contaminated recycle container can cause the entire truck load of material to be deemed contaminated and sends the entire load to the landfill.

sources.text: According to the EPA, here are the environmental and economic benefits of using landfill gas:  ENVIRONMENTAL BENEFITS  Landfill gas is a safe and renewable energy source.  Using landfill gas reduces the need to use more polluting forms of energy.  Using landfill gas reduces health and community risks, such as air pollution.  Landfills that use their landfill gas tend to be better managed and make better neighbors. -- 9 of 13 -- Gas to Energy Benefit BENEFITS  ECONOMIC BENEFITS  Landfill gas is a cost-effective, reliable, and local source of energy.  Using landfill gas can generate economic benefits for the community.  Developing and maintaining a landfill gas energy project creates local jobs.  A landfill with good power potential can attract business to the community. -- 10 of 13 -- Gas to Energy Benefit How It Works  According to the EPA, “When municipal solid waste is first deposited in a landfill, it undergoes an aerobic (with oxygen) decomposition stage when little methane is generated. Then, typically within less than 1 year, anaerobic conditions are established and methane-producing bacteria begin to decompose the waste and generate methane.  Landfill gas (LFG) is a natural byproduct of the decomposition of organic material in landfills. LFG is composed of roughly 50 percent methane (the primary component of natural gas), 50 percent carbon dioxide (CO2) and a small amount of non-methane organic compounds. -- 11 of 13 -- Gas to Energy Benefit How It Works  CONVERTING LANDFILL GAS TO ENERGY  Instead of escaping into the air, LFG can be captured, converted, and used as an energy source.

sources.text: Using LFG helps to reduce odors and other hazards associated with LFG emissions, and it helps prevent methane from migrating into the atmosphere.  LFG is extracted from landfills using a series of wells and a blower/flare (or vacuum) system. This system directs the collected gas to a central point where it can be transported, compressed, and filtered before it is combusted to generate electricity. -- 12 of 13 -- In Conclusion  Recycling right is the best way for Americans to protect the environment and stimulate the economy.  Recycling saves resource and reduces pollution.  Recycling is a shared responsibility.  Its easy! -- 13 of 13 --

sources.text: Water & Sewer Sterling Ranch water is provided by Dominion Water and Sanitation District, a wholesale water district serving Northwest Douglas County. To meet water demands, Dominion has contracts for permanent water delivery from Aurora Water, the Water Infrastructure and Supply Efficiency (WISE) project, and Castle Rock. Today, our water from contracts with the City of Aurora is delivered directly to the Larry D. Moore Water Treatment Plant, a facility jointly funded by Dominion and Roxborough Water and Sanitation District. Sterling Ranch: A Water-Wise Community The Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board ( CAB ) is committed to providing our residents with the highest quality tap water and reliable services. Sterling Ranch is part of a new approach to creating a regionally integrated, comprehensive water system with a robust, reliable, and renewable water supply. Dominion Water and Sanitation District and Sterling Ranch CAB have constructed a state-of-the-art water system, including a joint treatment facility with Roxborough Water and Sanitation District, the Larry D. Moore Water Treatment Plant. It is the first treatment plant in Colorado to receive 100% of its initial disinfection credits from Ultra Violet ( UV ) light and provides Sterling Ranch with clean, healthy water. Dominion Water and Sanitation District has been awarded a Certificate of Appreciation for being a WaterSense Partner by practicing and promoting water efficiency. Maintenance Checklist for a Water-Efficient Home Water & Sewer Billing After closing on their homes, Sterling Ranch residents are automatically set up for water and sewer services. Residents receive their water and sewer bills in the mail monthly and are billed in arrears.

sources.text: To learn more about WaterSense, visit www.epa.gov/watersense. 832-F-24-002 March 2024 Do This Once Per Year to Save Water:  Check your home for leaks (indoors and outdoors) and repair them promptly. Find instructions on WaterSense’s website at www.epa.gov/watersense/fix-leak-week.  Make sure your toilets aren’t continuously running. Check for leaks by putting a few drops of food coloring in the tank and wait 10 minutes; if color appears in the bowl, you have a leak. Flush afterwards to avoid staining.  Inspect showerheads and faucets for scale buildup and clean if necessary. sources.title: Water Billing
sources.text: Water Billing Sterling Ranch residents are automatically set up for water and sewer after closing on their homes. Residents receive their water and sewer bills in the mail monthly and are billed in arrears. American Conservation and Billing Solutions ( AmCoBi) administers the monthly water bill each month. Questions? AmCoBi's Client Care Services Team is available to assist you with questions or concerns regarding your water bill. Please contact them at: Toll-free: 1-833-SRCAB-40 or (833) 772-2240 E-mail: ClientCare@AmCoBi.com Payment Options: Please register your account through Utility Hawk ( https://srcab.utilityhawk.us ). Point your Web browser to: https://srcab.utilityhawk.us/login Select the "Pay Online" link on the home page. Follow the instructions. Your online account allows you to choose the best payment options for you, check your account balance and activity, and elect to receive your water bill electronically (eBill). AmCoBi's ePay service allows you to pay your bill online with an automatic withdrawal from your checking/savings account (ACH) free of charge. You can also use a debit or credit card with a processing fee of 2.95%, charged by Paymentus, the payment processing provider. Report a Water Concern If you have concerns or questions about the water in your home, please complete the Report a Water Concern Form and a staff member will be in touch with you. Contact Us Resident Resource Center info@sterlingranchcab.com Physical Address 8220 Piney River Avenue Sterling Ranch , CO 80125 Phone: 720-661-9694 Emergency Phone: 720-661-9694 Ext. 2

sources.title: Rent the Facility
sources.text: Rent the Facility The Overlook Clubhouse is an excellent venue to host your event. It provides a perfect location and a fantastic atmosphere for any occasion. The clubhouse is an ideal gathering space for organizing events, parties, community meetings, activities, picnics, groups, and clubs. The Member Services team at the Overlook Clubhouse will assist you in making your private party an event for you and your guests to remember! Great Hall The Overlook Clubhouse offers a Great Hall with a warming kitchen, an outdoor deck, and an indoor/outdoor fireplace. This space can be reserved for private use. However, when not reserved, the Great Hall, kitchen, and outdoor deck are available on a first-come, first-served basis. Please note that all members of the private rental must remain in the rented space, and additional facility access will not be permitted. Hourly Pricing $100.00 per hour with a 2-hour minimum. All rentals include the use of the indoor space and balcony. A refundable security deposit of 250.00 will also be due upon rental confirmation. Outdoor Pavilions The clubhouse has two outdoor, covered pavilions to reserve for private parties. The pavilions are available on a first-come, first-served basis when not reserved for private use. Each household can reserve one of the outdoor pavilions once per day, with no more than two rentals per calendar month. All members of the private rental must stay in the rented space. Additional facility access is not permitted. North Pavilion Larger space that includes an outdoor fireplace and convertible picnic tables South Pavilion Smaller space that includes an outdoor BBQ grill and two picnic tables Hourly Pricing $25 per hour.

sources.text: All categories Home - FAQs Water Water Communication Retrofit Design Review Compliance Overlook Clubhouse Pool Frequently Asked Questions Water 6 All Content What does the monthly fixed fee include? The water rate billing structure includes a fixed monthly water service base fee and a residential usage charge. This base fee covers the cost of the water and sewer utility’s fixed and operating costs before any service is provided. The residential usage charge is based on tiered rates and are variable based upon use. Rates and Fees are established annually by the Community Authority Board (CAB) Board. The CAB rates are generally higher than many of the neighboring utilities and does not include a mill levy component that many neighboring utilities use to fund capital projects. However, many of these neighboring providers are older, established enterprises who rely on nonrenewable water supplies. The CAB rates are based on developing a renewable water system from inception. It is likely water rates for neighboring utilities will continue to rise at a faster rate than those of the CAB due to the costs of obtaining and developing renewable water supplies. Water How are my indoor water usage tiers established? A homeowner’s individualized indoor water budget is structured on an average winter consumption ( AWC ) to determine the tier 1 threshold. The AWC is determined by averaging the customer’s actual indoor water use for the months of December, January, and February. The AWC is reset annually to allow for life changes. The tier 1 minimum threshold for residential homes is a minimum of 4,000 gallons per month and a maximum of 6,000 gallons per month. Accounts without an AWC history will be assigned 6,000 gallons per month as an initial AWC .

sources.text: Water How do I troubleshoot your water meter when you have no water? Valves - Gen 1 These valves require the smart home system to be online and functioning to open and close the valves. To troubleshoot we recommend the following: Make sure the smart home system is online; if not, use https://lumiere.technology/knowledge-base/category/STEWARD/ Submit a ticket with our team at https://lumiere.technology/open-a-ticket/ Water Valves - Gen 2 These valves can easily be opened and closed manually. To troubleshoot, we recommend the following: Click the blue power button on the Dome Valve 1 time. 1 click will cause the arm to turn and open the water supply (see Gen 2 Valves #2 for that power button) If this button does not cause the arm to turn, pull the silver pin on the device and manually move the arm (see Gen 2 Valves #3 for that pin) For additional help submit a ticket at https://lumiere.technology/open-a-ticket/ Water Why are outdoor water rates slightly higher than indoor water rates? The water rates are structured to recover system costs. Outdoor water rates were designed to encourage water-wise irrigation practices. Outdoor water use increases the demand on our water system, and therefore the operational costs of our facilities. Additionally, when water is used outdoors it is fully consumed and not returned to the system. Water How do I move into higher tiers each month? The first tier of fee rates per 1,000 gallons applies to the use of up to 100% of the customer’s water budget. The tier fee rate per 1,000 gallons for use over 100% of the water budget increases based upon the amount over 100% that is used by that customer.

sources.text: All categories Home - FAQs Water Water Communication Retrofit Design Review Compliance Overlook Clubhouse Pool Frequently Asked Questions Overlook Clubhouse Pool 9 All Content What are the pool rules? All swimmers must check in at the front desk with their membership card or a photo of it. There is no pool entrance from the side gates. Children under the age of 11 years must be accompanied and actively supervised by a parent, guardian, or if authorized by a parent/guardian, another individual of 15 years of age or older, while using the Clubhouse or Pool. Swimming any time where a lifeguard is not on duty is at the swimmer's sole risk. Lifeguards may not be on duty when temperatures are below 65 degrees and inclement weather is present. All users must take a cleansing shower before entering the pool. Showering after using the pool is recommended. Appropriate swimwear must be worn at all times. Street clothing (basketball shorts, jean/denim materials, cargo shorts), undergarments, sports bras, or similar attire is prohibited in the pool. White t-shirts or tank-tops are permitted in the pool if worn over appropriate swim attire. Pool staff will make the final determination if swimwear is appropriate. Nudity is strictly prohibited. Non-swimmers must be accompanied by a swimmer in the water and be within an arm's reach at all times. Glass containers are prohibited in the pool and pool areas. Food and beverages are permitted on the pool deck. Food and beverages are not permitted in the pool. To avoid spilling food or beverages into the pool, please keep them at your chair or table. Users who are ill, have experienced vomiting or diarrhea in the past 24 hours, have open sores, or ear/nasal discharge should not use the pool.

sources.text: Swim diapers must be worn by all incontinent swimmers. Horseplay, running, diving into the pool, and hanging/swinging/pulling on aquatic equipment or features is prohibited. Repeat violators will be asked to leave the pool. Lane lines, stairs, and railings are installed to assist and guide pool users. Standing, hanging from, or sitting on these items is prohibited. Inflatable pool toys, flotation aids, or similar items are only allowed under the following conditions: Only transparent, circular inflatables no larger than 42 inches in diameter, infant inflatables, water wings with an attached chest piece, and pool noodles are permitted in the pool. Mesh infant inflatables may be no larger than 33 inches by 38 inches. Pool mattresses or other inflatables are prohibited. Users with noncompliant inflatables or flotation devices will be asked to remove them from the pool. Personal sound equipment, such as stereos or wireless speakers, are permitted as long as they do not disrupt others' enjoyment of the pool. If any complaints are received, Users will be asked to turn down their music, use headphones, or upon repeated complaint, asked to turn off the device or leave the pool. The pool must be cleared during thunder and lightning storms or other inclement weather events that present danger to Users.

sources.text: If you haven’t signed up to get access to the Overlook Clubhouse, complete the Resident Amenity Form online today! **For homeowners who registered for the Overlook Clubhouse prior to its opening in October 2020 should have received the email to complete account setup already. If you have not received the email or your link is expired, please contact the Overlook Clubhouse at 720-728-7257 or email recreation@sterlingranchcab.com and a staff member will assist you.** This account and password are for the new CIVICREC system and will be used for registering for events, reserving time to use the fitness center, purchasing fitness classes, additional guest passes, and more! Follow the instructions listed below to complete your account setup. How to Finish Your Online Account Setup Open the email. You will have a username (your email provided) and a temporary password to log in. Select TO LOGIN AND CHANGE YOUR PASSWORD NOW CLICK HERE. You will be redirected to the new CIVICREC Website. Once logged in, select ACCOUNT in the top lefthand corner. Select the pencil icon next to your name. In the lower-left corner, select RESET CIVICREC PASSWORD. You will be prompted to confirm that you would like to reset the password. A password reset link will be sent to your email. Follow the instructions to reset your password. Registering for Events & Programs Navigate to the Community Calendar . Click on the event that interests you. Click "More Details" to view the full event description, event cost, suggested ages, and registration links. Review the event details and confirm if an RSVP or program registration is required. If required, a link to register on the right-hand column will say "Register Now" Follow the registration prompts.

sources.text: The residential usage charge is based on tiered rates and are variable based upon use. Rates and Fees are established annually by the Community Authority Board (CAB) Board. The CAB rates are generally higher than many of the neighboring utilities and does not include a mill levy component that many neighboring utilities use to fund capital projects. However, many of these neighboring providers are older, established enterprises who rely on nonrenewable water supplies. The CAB rates are based on developing a renewable water system from inception. It is likely water rates for neighboring utilities will continue to rise at a faster rate than those of the CAB due to the costs of obtaining and developing renewable water supplies. Water How are my indoor water usage tiers established? A homeowner’s individualized indoor water budget is structured on an average winter consumption ( AWC ) to determine the tier 1 threshold. The AWC is determined by averaging the customer’s actual indoor water use for the months of December, January, and February. The AWC is reset annually to allow for life changes. The tier 1 minimum threshold for residential homes is a minimum of 4,000 gallons per month and a maximum of 6,000 gallons per month. Accounts without an AWC history will be assigned 6,000 gallons per month as an initial AWC . Water How do I troubleshoot your water meter when you have no water? Valves - Gen 1 These valves require the smart home system to be online and functioning to open and close the valves.

sources.text: Once the Siemens technician arrives at your home, the equipment upgrades should take approximately 2 hours. Water Communication Retrofit Will I be able to use internet while the upgrade is taking place? The technician will need to shut off a circuit breaker to perform the necessary electrical work. If your internet is utilizing that same circuit breaker, you will not be able to access the internet for approximately 45 minutes while electrical work is being performed. Because of this, we strongly recommend not scheduling critical tasks that will require internet access or VoIP phone use during your service window. Water Communication Retrofit What can I do to prepare? In order to minimize the time required, prior to the technician’s arrival please clear adequate space (at least 3 square feet) around your water meter panel, electrical breaker box, and STEWARD equipment. This equipment is typically located in the basement. If you do not have a basement, the equipment is typically located in the garage. Water Communication Retrofit What information should I be ready to share? If you have changed the default login to your CenturyLink ONT /modem’s admin portal, please be prepared to provide that information as well. If you would prefer not to share this information, please be prepared to input your credentials for the technician at the necessary times. If you do not know your STEWARD login credentials, visit the Lumiere website . Water Communication Retrofit Why are you removing the virtual private network (VPN) hardware? The virtual private network ( VPN ) hardware was previously necessary to ensure proper encryption of water meter information during transmission to the water billing system. This is no longer the case as we are now able to use an alternate encryption method.

sources.text: Application fees can be paid via check made payable to Sterling Ranch CAB, or via credit/debit card. Please contact the team at the Resident Resource Center for assistance paying via credit/debit card. Checks can be mailed or dropped off to Sterling Ranch CAB, 8220 Piney River Ave, Littleton, CO 80125. Design Review After I receive my approval, can I modify or deviate from my application slightly? Approval was granted based on the information the homeowner provided to the committee on the application. A new Design Review Application will need to be submitted should a homeowner need to make any changes to the original application. (EXCEPT for plant material selection as long as it is for water to water same) Design Review How long does the Design Review Process take? The Design Review Committee has up to 30 days to review a submittal from the date a completed submittal package was received at the Design Review Committee meeting. If you have not been notified in writing by the 31st day after the meeting, the submittal is deemed to be denied. It is the responsibility of the applicant to contact the Design Review Committee to determine the status of the submittal. Design Review How many days do I have to install my rear yard? The rear yard landscape must be completed within 120 days following your closing. A Winter Deferral Period for completion of rear yard planting is granted for closings from November 1 to April 30. Design Review Am I allowed to make changes to my grading or drainage? The DRC does not evaluate changes to grading or drainage. Applicants are to seek approval from the County and/or other appropriate governing bodies. The DRC is not responsible in any way for changes made to grading and/or drainage while installing landscaping or other improvements.

The recommend plant list is a great start to understanding the Sterling Ranch planting palette, but the Design Review Committee will review additional plant material requests. Design Review Am I limited to the landscape contractors on the Pre-Approved Landscaper List? No, you may work with a landscaper of your choice, but that professional landscaper will need to meet with our Architectural and Community Standards Director to become certified and approved. The approval process includes education on Sterling Ranch Water Demand Management Initiatives and the Design Review process. Please note, inclusion on this list does not constitute the CAB’s endorsement of any of these companies. Learn more about Design Review Compliance Are there any guidelines I need to follow to have a temporary dumpster or a storage pod at my house? Please submit an Application for General Architectural Improvements to the Design Review Committee for approval. Include with the application timeframe for dumpster or storage pod to be at property. Please note, dumpsters and storage pods must be placed in your driveway and are not allowed on a public right-of-way per Douglas County officials. Compliance What is the guideline for having a recreational vehicle at my home? The maximum amount of time a Recreational Vehicle is allowed to be parked is three overnights (e.g., 72 hours) during any 7-day period for loading, delivery, and maintenance. Periodic movement of the vehicle for the purpose of circumventing this standard shall not qualify the vehicle for an exception from this standard. Please refer to the Residential Property Owner Guidebook, Article VI General Standards for further regulation details. Compliance Do I need to submit my paint colors even if I am painting my home the exact same colors? DRC approval is required, even if re-painting is being done with the same colors as the original or previous paint color. Please refer to the Residential Property Owner Guidebook, Article VI General Standards for further regulation details. Compliance Do trampolines and play equipment require approval? DRC approval is required. Trampolines will be considered based on size, height, color, relationship to size of lot, relationship to landscaping, setbacks from property lines, method of installation, and proposed safety netting. Trampolines are required to be anchored per manufacturer specifications.

sources.text: Compliance Is it okay for me to access the open space to do improvements on my property? No, all access to your property must be from the street side at the front of your home. Accessing the property through another lot, open space, parks, or landscaped tracts is prohibited. Please refer to the Residential Property Owner Guidebook, Section IV. Landscaping Standards. Compliance What can I do about a barking dog or a neighbor that does not clean up after their animals on a regular basis? If you are trying to solve a problem with a barking dog or clean up after a pet, please start with communicating your concern to the pet owner or contact the following county authorities: Douglas County Animal Services, 303-660-7529, 7:00 a.m. - 6:00 p.m. Sheriff’s Department Dispatch, 303-660-7500 (After 6 p.m. if an animal problem requires immediate attention). Compliance Overlook Clubhouse Pool 9 All Content What are the pool rules? All swimmers must check in at the front desk with their membership card or a photo of it. There is no pool entrance from the side gates. Children under the age of 11 years must be accompanied and actively supervised by a parent, guardian, or if authorized by a parent/guardian, another individual of 15 years of age or older, while using the Clubhouse or Pool. Swimming any time where a lifeguard is not on duty is at the swimmer's sole risk. Lifeguards may not be on duty when temperatures are below 65 degrees and inclement weather is present. All users must take a cleansing shower before entering the pool. Showering after using the pool is recommended. Appropriate swimwear must be worn at all times. Street clothing (basketball shorts, jean/denim materials, cargo shorts), undergarments, sports bras, or similar attire is prohibited in the pool.

sources.text: White t-shirts or tank-tops are permitted in the pool if worn over appropriate swim attire. Pool staff will make the final determination if swimwear is appropriate. Nudity is strictly prohibited. Non-swimmers must be accompanied by a swimmer in the water and be within an arm's reach at all times. Glass containers are prohibited in the pool and pool areas. Food and beverages are permitted on the pool deck. Food and beverages are not permitted in the pool. To avoid spilling food or beverages into the pool, please keep them at your chair or table. Users who are ill, have experienced vomiting or diarrhea in the past 24 hours, have open sores, or ear/nasal discharge should not use the pool. Swim diapers must be worn by all incontinent swimmers. Horseplay, running, diving into the pool, and hanging/swinging/pulling on aquatic equipment or features is prohibited. Repeat violators will be asked to leave the pool. Lane lines, stairs, and railings are installed to assist and guide pool users. Standing, hanging from, or sitting on these items is prohibited. When lap lanes are present, those areas are for lap swimming and water walking only. During busy times, lap swimmers may be asked to share lanes, circle swim, or limit swim time to ensure all have an opportunity to use the facilities. The pool deck is reserved for walking, safety, and emergency purposes. No obstruction of any kind will be permitted in this area. Inflatable pool toys, flotation aids, or similar items are only allowed under the following conditions: Only transparent, circular inflatables no larger than 42 inches in diameter, infant inflatables, water wings with an attached chest piece, and pool noodles are permitted in the pool. Mesh infant inflatables may be no larger than 33 inches by 38 inches.

sources.text: 8155 Piney River Ave #150, Littleton CO 80125 Billing Inquiries: Clientcare@amcobi.com Welcome, Sterling Ranch residents, to the most advanced water conservation community in Colorado. We are committed to conserving water and being good stewards of the land. Our innovative water solutions to conserve water community-wide will help residents with water costs long term. You play a part in this important conservation and we need your help. As you get your rear yards planted, we understand the need for an Establishment Period to promote healthy root system growth. This Rear Yard Establishment Period is a one-time only, 45-day period following the date of completion of your rear landscaping. Outdoor water used during this Rear Yard Establishment Period will be billed at the most affordable water cost, which is the “Tier One” water rate. In addition, the amount of water delivered during the Rear Yard Establishment Period will not count against your overall Water Budget. Please let the Community Authority Board know of your need for the Rear Yard Establishment Period water rates by completing the form below so that we make sure to ensure proper billing. This form can be mailed to the CAB at the address listed above or emailed to Clientcare@amcobi.com Name Address Phone Number Email Address Closing Date Account Number DATE OF TURF/VEGETATION COMPLETION OWNER SIGNATURE DATE CONDITIONS: 1. Due to the time needed to process this Notification, Tier One credits will be applied one time to your water bill at the end of the 45-day period. 2. Owners have 1-year to apply for Establishment Period credits. The 1-year period will start on the 120th day following Closing.

sources.text: Sterling Ranch Residential Property Owner Guidebook August 26, 2020 {00488209} Page 50 ATTACHMENT B-3 - REQUEST FOR LANDSCAPING INSPECTIONS The Sterling Ranch Water Demand Management Initiatives * specify that soil amendment must be inspected prior to planting. This is to verify amendments have been incorporated into the soil in the quantity specified and to the depth required. Per the Water Demand Management Initiatives, the specification is 4 cubic yards of soil amendment for each 1000 square feet, tilled to a depth of 6 inches. Soil Amendment must be a combination of aged ground manure and compost. A second inspection will be performed after irrigation and plantings are complete in order to verify that the installed material is in substantial conformance with the approved plans, and that the irrigation system is active and in substantial conformance with the approved plans. The fee payment for these inspections is as follows: . $100.00 This fee covers both Soil Amendment Inspection and Landscape/Irrigation Inspection . Fee Payments should be made payable to Sterling Ranch Community Authority and sent to: Sterling Ranch Community Authority 8155 Piney River Ave, #150 Littleton CO 80125 TO SCHEDULE AN INSPECTION (MINIMUM 48 HOURS NOTICE, MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY ONLY): Contact residentialinspections@sterlingranchcab.com Provide your name, phone number, and email address plus the address of the property to be inspected. * If you do not have a copy of the Water Demand Management Initiatives, please visit www.sterlingranchcab.com to download the document. -- 1 of 1 --

sources.text: Sterling Ranch Code of Rules May 25, 2023 {00488209} Page 65 Registrations may be granted via reciprocity to individuals who hold registrations in other Colorado municipalities, on a case-by-case basis, as deemed appropriate by the Community Authority Board (“CAB”). AN APPLICANT MUST DEMONSTRATE THAT HE/SHE MEETS THE REQUIREMENTS BY PROVIDING CURRENT PROOF OF PROFESSIONAL QUALIFICATIONS. IN THE ABSENCE OF THESE CREDENTIALS, AN APPLICANT MAY SUBMIT A NARRATIVE LISTING THREE MOST RECENT PROJECTS, DOLLAR AMOUNT, COMPLETION DATE, AND CONTACT INFORMATION FOR THE PERSON FOR WHOM THE PROJECT WAS DONE. The CAB reserves the right to deny, suspend, or revoke any registration in accordance with its policies. ATTACHMENT G APPLICATION FOR APPROVAL OF LANDSCAPE PROFESSIONALS Registration requirements apply companies or organizations, not to individuals. The registered company or organization is responsible for all work performed under its supervision. Colorado law governs the sizes and types of projects that unlicensed individuals can design, and is independent from CAB policies. Registrations are valid for a period of three (3) years. Registration renewals for professionals in good standing may be issued upon receipt of acknowledgment of revisions to policies, criteria, or other applicable codes. Non-compliance with these policies may deem an applicant ineligible for renewal or result in an applicant’s removal from the approval list.

sources.title: Calculating Outdoor Water Usage
sources.text: 8155 Piney River Avenue, #150 | Littleton Colorado 80125 submit@sterlingranchdrc.com Calculating Outdoor Water Usage for a Landscape Design Every home in Sterling Ranch has an outdoor water use budget based on the overall lot square footage. For water offered at the lowest, Tier 1 billing rate, see Table 1 below. . 30% of the outdoor water budget is used by the builder for the front yard irrigation . 70% of the overall outdoor water budget remains to irrigate the backyard plants . It is recommended to not design a landscape that requires 100% of the budget to allow for seasons with high temperatures and little precipitation conditions so that the Tier 1 billing rate is not exceeded. Calculate Outdoor Water Use Determine which plants in the plan are High Water, Moderate Water, and Low Water usage. Local nursery websites are a great resource to help understand the water needs of plants. Sod, vegetable gardens, and water features are always high water usage. Then, begin calculating the irrigated square footage (sf) of the plant by using the sf of each plant at full growth. See calculations below for some typical plant sizes. Trees are the exception to the rule. As water is only delivered around the trunk of the tree, use a 3’ diameter irrigated area for calculations. -- 1 of 2 -- 8155 Piney River Avenue, #150 | Littleton Colorado 80125 submit@sterlingranchdrc.com High Water Use: plant irrigated sf x 20 gals/sf = Total gallons needed for the season Moderate Water Use: plant irrigated sf x 10 gals/sf = Total gallons needed for the season Low Water Use: plant irrigated sf x 6 gals/sf = Total gallons needed for the season For example, a Moderate Water use plant at 2’ diameter full growth: 3.142 sf irrigated area x 10 gals/sf = 31.42 gallons needed for the season.

Please review all Community governing documents prior to planning any modifications to the exterior of your home. 8220 Piney River Avenue | Littleton, Colorado 80125 | www.sterlingranchcab.com OUTDOOR CONTROLLED PET AREAS DRC approval is required for all outdoor controlled pet areas including dog runs and kennels. . All outdoor controlled areas must be located in the side or rear yard, abutting the home and located behind yard fencing. . May not be located in a side yard adjacent to corner sidewalk, street, common area or open space. . Must be substantially screened from view by fast-growing plant material. Evergreen plantings and grasses are required for four season screening. . Required to be kept in a clean, sanitary condition, and not allowed to fall into disrepair. Please be aware Sterling Ranch is home to various different types of wildlife. Always recommend, household pets including dogs and cats be kept indoors for their safety. Dog Run . A fenced, open-top area . May not exceed 200 square feet or more than 25% of the rear yard, whichever is less, . Constructed of fencing material matching that of lot-line fencing and stained to match lot-line fencing or may be black powder-coated steel not to exceed 48” in height from grade at any point. . Metal chain link enclosures are not permitted. . Pet mesh screen is required to be 2” x 4” galvanized welded wire mesh used on the inside of the fence, not to exceed the top rail in height, and continued down to ground level. . Covers (ex: tarps, sheets, blankets, etc.) are NOT allowed. Kennel . A free-standing panel-system kennel may not exceed 50 square feet and must be a maximum of 48 inches in height. .

sources.text: The information on this sheet is NOT all inclusive of all Community Design Guidelines or Covenants. Please review all Community governing documents prior to planning any modifications to the exterior of your home. 8220 Piney River Avenue | Littleton, Colorado 80125 | www.sterlingranchcab.com LANDSCAPE SCREENS DRC approval is required for landscape screens and will be considered based on the location of the screens, the size of your yard and the impact of screens on neighbors and the community. . 5’ maximum overall height for exposed landscape screen from grade. If plantings are installed at the base of the screen, facing out toward the community view, screen height will be allowed at a 6’ maximum overall height from grade. . 8’ maximum overall width for landscape screens. Multiple screens may not be attached at corners, at edges, to sheds, or to the house. Must be freestanding in the rear or side yard. . Landscape screens are only allowed in rear or side yards and are not allowed in easements. A maximum of three (3) screens are allowed if lot square footage permits. The DRC will review on a case by case basis. . Landscape screens must have 30% required transparency. . Materials must be constructed of a minimum 50% top grade redwood or cedar, or high grade Trex material or an equivalent in a color complementary to the home. If other materials like masonry or metal are used, they must match the architectural style of the house. Vinyl is not permitted. . Landscape screens may be either painted or stained. Paint colors must match or compliment house colors. Stain must match fence stain (Sherwin Williams #3002 Belvedere Tan) or a natural stain. Wood grain is allowed to show through. . Landscape screens may be used to screen hot tub areas on two sides only. .

Please review all Community governing documents prior to planning any modifications to the exterior of your home. 8220 Piney River Avenue | Littleton, Colorado 80125 | www.sterlingranchcab.com TRASH ENCLOSURE/SCREENING Trash bins need to be kept within garages or in an approved enclosure. Keep the neighborhood beautiful and completely screen unsightly trash and recycling bins from view from the street, the sidewalk or any adjacent property. DRC approval is NOT REQUIRED if ALL of the following conditions are met: . The trash enclosure/screening is installed behind the wing fence in the side yard (may not be on an exposed corner side), . Must be attached to the side of the house, . Has a minimum setback from the side property line of 5 feet, . Is not located within any easement(s), . Is constructed of top-grade cedar or high grade Trex material or an equivalent in a color complementary to the home or painted to match the fence stain color of Sherwin Williams #3002 “Belvedere Tan,” and . May not exceed 4’-6” in height from ground level at any point. Any trash enclosure/screening not meeting ALL of these conditions must be submitted for DRC approval. Trash and Recycling enclosures will be considered based on size, height, color, relationship to size of lot, relationship to landscaping, and setbacks from property lines. Material, style and color, including roofing, need to be appropriate for the architectural style of the home. Please be aware Sterling Ranch is home to various different types of wildlife! Proper trash cart storage is important to the safety of the community and those that inhabit it.

An open-rail fence consisting of 3 concrete rails and concrete vertical posts per community specifications (can be downloaded at www.sterlingranchcab.com) with integral coloring in Solomon #338 “Earthen.” . All interior lot line fencing must be stained and kept in good repair. ADDITIONAL GATES Requests will only be considered for additional gates located within front wing fencing, interior lot line fencing between two homes if both neighbors are in agreement, signatures required on submittal plan drawings, or rear perimeter fencing when adjacent to CAB owned common space with CAB permission. Additional gates within side and rear property line concrete fencing that are street facing are not allowed.

Please submit your completed application digitally via residentsubmit@sterlingranchcab.com Design Review Committee (DRC) meetings are scheduled for the first and third Thursday during the months of March through September, and the first Thursday during October through February. Applications and forms can be downloaded on the DRC Applications web page . Completed applications must be received via residentsubmit@sterlingranchcab.com by end of business day on the Friday prior to a DRC meeting to be reviewed at that meeting. If it is not received by end of business on the Friday before the meeting, it will be put on the following meeting’s agenda. If a fee is required, mail the physical check made out to Sterling Ranch Community Authority along with a copy of your application to Sterling Ranch DRC, 8155 Piney River Avenue, Suite 150, Littleton, CO 80125. sources.text: Login to your Sterling Ranch Utility account at https://ebill.sterlingranchco.com/ubs1/ to: Pay your bill or setup an automatic payment Review your 12-month usage summary Understand your gallon consumption by month and year If you are having trouble locating your account number or need a copy of your bill please email info@sterlingranchcab.com Quarterly Assessment Bill: The quarterly CAB Service Fees are billed on a quarterly basis and are administered by Capital Consultants Management Corporation ( CCMC ). Quarterly CAB Service Fees include stormwater, trash and recycling, streetlights, and driveway maintenance (Lennar Elements homes only). Payment options are listed below. Direct-Debit The direct-debit payment option is available at no charge. If you are set up for direct-debit and your assessment has changed, the new amount will automatically be deducted. Download and complete the direct debit authorization form. Electronic Checks & Credit Card Payments To pay by Credit Card or Electronic, visit the Smartstreet Website . There is a $14.95 processing fee per credit card transaction. There is no charge for electronic check transactions. American Express, Discover, Mastercard, and Visa are accepted. Recurring credit card payments with Smartstreet are valid for one year or when your credit card expires, whichever is sooner. At that time, you must renew your payment with Smartstreet, it does not happen automatically. If you have recurring payments with Smartstreet and your assessment amount changes, you must update your payment information with Smartstreet as it doesn’t happen automatically. Bill-Payment Services If you use a bill-payment service please review your account number and payment mailing address.

sources.text: If you haven’t signed up to get access to the Overlook Clubhouse, complete the Resident Amenity Form online today! **For homeowners who registered for the Overlook Clubhouse prior to its opening in October 2020 should have received the email to complete account setup already. If you have not received the email or your link is expired, please contact the Overlook Clubhouse at 720-728-7257 or email recreation@sterlingranchcab.com and a staff member will assist you.** This account and password are for the new CIVICREC system and will be used for registering for events, reserving time to use the fitness center, purchasing fitness classes, additional guest passes, and more! Follow the instructions listed below to complete your account setup. How to Finish Your Online Account Setup Open the email. You will have a username (your email provided) and a temporary password to log in. Select TO LOGIN AND CHANGE YOUR PASSWORD NOW CLICK HERE. You will be redirected to the new CIVICREC Website. Once logged in, select ACCOUNT in the top lefthand corner. Select the pencil icon next to your name. In the lower-left corner, select RESET CIVICREC PASSWORD. You will be prompted to confirm that you would like to reset the password. A password reset link will be sent to your email. Follow the instructions to reset your password. Registering for Events & Programs Navigate to the Community Calendar . Click on the event that interests you. Click "More Details" to view the full event description, event cost, suggested ages, and registration links. Review the event details and confirm if an RSVP or program registration is required. If required, a link to register on the right-hand column will say "Register Now" Follow the registration prompts.

Home - FAQs How do I trouble shoot your water meter when you have no water? Valves - Gen 1 These valves require the smart home system to be online and functioning to open and close the valves. To troubleshoot we recommend the following: Make sure the smart home system is online; if not, use https://lumiere.technology/knowledge-base/category/STEWARD/ Submit a ticket with our team at https://lumiere.technology/open-a-ticket/ Water Valves - Gen 2 These valves can easily be opened and closed manually. To troubleshoot, we recommend the following: Click the blue power button on the Dome Valve 1 time. 1 click will cause the arm to turn and open the water supply (see Gen 2 Valves #2 for that power button) If this button does not cause the arm to turn, pull the silver pin on the device and manually move the arm (see Gen 2 Valves #3 for that pin) For additional help submit a ticket at https://lumiere.technology/open-a-ticket/ Home - FAQs Home - FAQs 6 How do I submit an application for Design Review? sources.text: STEWARD Home Automation System STEWARD is your Smart Home Automation System and tightly integrated with all your other in-home devices. It’s an all-in-one home automation, home security, and utility monitoring system that came standard with your new Sterling Ranch home. STEWARD works with voice control, smart thermostats, door locks, garage doors, security cameras, and more. Standard Features Real-time, hourly & monthly reporting of your natural gas, electric & water usage A Rachio smart irrigation controller configured to water your lawn efficiently A DSC home security system that is connected to the STEWARD system Automated lighting and HVAC controls Connection to the Sterling Ranch Community to keep you informed about what’s happening around the neighborhood!
